solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: One holding groceries and dancing lively dance for Spooner (8,3)

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the phrase is said his way

blocks.note: bopping is dancing; it hands its B to the next word and takes SH in return
the shag is a lively swing dance; its SH swaps with the B

annotation.surface: Someone out shopping bops along, groceries in hand.
annotation.walkthrough: The shag is a lively swing dance of the 1930s and 40s; swapping the openings of BOPPING SHAG gives the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A shopping bag is exactly the thing that holds your groceries.

entries.clue: Silverware half-heartedly put on gold support (7)

indicators.note: the heart of SPOONS is OO, and half of it goes
in a down clue the first part sits on top of the second

blocks.note: SPOONS losing one of its two central Os
OR is gold in heraldry

annotation.surface: Silver cutlery set, rather listlessly, on a golden stand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Support' looks like a noun at the end of the surface, but it works as the verb: to sponsor someone is to back them.
annotation.definitionFit: To sponsor someone is to support them, often with money.

entries.clue: Now and again, go wrong as trek is not simple (6)

indicators.note: only now and then, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the even letters: gO wRoNg As TrEk

annotation.walkthrough: 'Go wrong' tempts you to look for an anagram indicator; here it is simply part of the fodder whose every second letter is taken.
annotation.surface: A hike that sometimes goes astray proves complicated.
annotation.definitionFit: Something ornate is elaborate, the opposite of simple.

entries.clue: Parking supplementing new train station (10)

blocks.note: P is the parking sign
supplementing is adding to
N is the standard abbreviation for new

annotation.surface: Extra car parking is added at a newly opened railway station.
annotation.walkthrough: Paddington is a main-line railway terminus in London.
annotation.definitionFit: Paddington is one of London's big railway stations.

entries.clue: Question ultimately raised in public denial (4)

indicators.note: at the end, so the last letter of 'Question'
the N already at the bottom of OPEN is lifted to the top, which in a down answer is the start

blocks.note: last letter of QuestioN
OPEN, with its final N the one taken up to the top

annotation.surface: A final question, brought up in public, meets a flat refusal.
annotation.walkthrough: Public is OPEN; its final N, which is also the last letter of 'Question', moves from the foot of the down answer to the head.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in casual speech: saying no to something is denying it.

entries.clue: Prominence of Cyrano de Bergerac with involvement of one VIP (3,5)

indicators.note: one is involved in, so placed inside, the other

blocks.note: Cyrano is famous for his very large nose
I is the Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: Cyrano's famous nose makes him stand out as a very important person.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prominence' reads as fame, but here it is literally the part that sticks out: Cyrano's big nose.
annotation.definitionFit: A big noise is slang for an important person, a VIP.

entries.clue: Fellow eats last of Cheddar before Swiss cheese (7)

indicators.note: the first part swallows the second
the final letter of 'Cheddar'

blocks.note: a guy is a fellow
last letter of CheddaR
ere is an old word for before

annotation.surface: A man finishes the Cheddar before moving on to a Swiss cheese.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Before' looks like a time link in the surface, but it supplies ERE, the old poetic word for before.
annotation.definitionFit: Gruyère is a hard cheese from Switzerland.

entries.clue: Brother on vacation had tanned (7)

indicators.note: vacated, emptied of its middle, leaving the outer letters

blocks.note: BROTHER emptied
to have something is to own it

annotation.surface: A brother comes back from holiday with a suntan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' tempts you to think of holidays and suntans, but it tells you to empty BROTHER.
annotation.definitionFit: Browned and tanned both describe skin darkened by the sun.

entries.clue: Life begins at forty: resolved to leave for sea organised appropriately (11)

indicators.note: broken down and made again, so the letters are rearranged
the letters of the next words depart from the fodder
the letters of 'for sea' can be removed in any order, not as a run

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 17 letters
these six letters are taken out, leaving 11 to rearrange

annotation.surface: Someone turning forty decides to leave for the sea, all neatly arranged.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole saying is the fodder. The letters of FOR SEA are not together in it, so they are removed one by one before the rest is rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Befittingly means in a way that suits the occasion, appropriately.

entries.clue: Dick hurt back getting edible tubers (7)

indicators.note: the word for hurt is written backwards

blocks.note: a private dick is a private investigator, a PI
STUNG, reversed

annotation.surface: A man called Dick hurts his back digging up something to eat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dick' looks like a man's name; it is slang for a detective.
annotation.definitionFit: Pignuts are the small edible tubers of a wild plant, dug up by foragers.

entries.clue: What salesperson at marina might do displays theatricality (11)

definitions.text: What salesperson at marina might do

blocks.clueFragment: What salesperson at marina might do
blocks.note: a cryptic hint: a boat dealer shows a customer round a vessel, split into three words

annotation.surface: A boat salesman puts on quite a show for his customers.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic hint: a boat dealer might SHOW a MAN a SHIP.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a flair for performance and display is theatricality, while the split reading gives the literal sales pitch.

entries.clue: Break down about this novel’s bleak end, perhaps (4,4)

indicators.note: goes around the other part
new, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: a machine that breaks down fails
THIS rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone collapses over the grim ending of a book.
annotation.walkthrough: A bleak is a small river fish, so its end is a fish's tail; the surface sells 'bleak' as gloomy and 'novel' as a book.
annotation.definitionFit: The end of a bleak, a small fish, is a fish tail; 'perhaps' flags the example.

entries.clue: Jacket having bad smell worn by character cycling (6)

indicators.note: the smell is put on, inside, the character
letters go round from the front to the back

blocks.note: a character in a play is a role
BO is body odour

annotation.surface: A jacket that smells from being worn by someone on a bike.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' suggests a bicycle, but it tells you to rotate the letters: after the insertion, the first two move round to the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: this short, open-fronted garment, cut above the waist, is a type of jacket.

entries.clue: Scan a photo possibly showing Native American woman (10)

indicators.note: the letters could possibly be arranged another way

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: Digitising an old photograph of a Native American woman.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder runs across three words, and the definition by example names the most famous Native American woman in popular memory.
annotation.definitionFit: Pocahontas was a Powhatan woman famous from early Virginia.

entries.clue: Picked up routine flier (4)

indicators.note: heard, as a radio picks up a signal

blocks.note: a turn is a performer's routine

annotation.surface: Someone collects a regular leaflet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flier' looks like a leaflet, but it is a bird; a turn is an act in a variety show.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this seabird is one of many things that fly, and 'flier' hides behind its leaflet sense.

entries.clue: Extraordinary mega-fast gains primarily escalated over industrialisation period (3,2,5)

indicators.note: out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged
'primarily' means in the first place, so each word gives only the letter in its first place

blocks.note: anagram fodder
first letters of Escalated Over

annotation.surface: Very rapid gains shot up during the Industrial Revolution.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gains' joins the two parts: the anagram fodder gains E and O.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for the Industrial Revolution, when steam engines powered factories and railways.

entries.clue: On high netting starts to rig tackle of vessel (8)

indicators.note: catching, so holding the other part inside
the first letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: aerial means up in the air
first letters of Rig Tackle

annotation.surface: Up aloft, sailors net the rigging and tackle of a boat.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sells 'vessel' as a ship; it is a blood vessel.
annotation.definitionFit: Arterial means relating to an artery, a kind of blood vessel.

entries.clue: Shrimpers on a lagoon somewhat cold (10)

indicators.note: only some of the words, so the answer is a part of them

blocks.note: shrIMPERS ON A Lagoon

annotation.surface: People catching shrimp on a lagoon feel a bit chilly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cold' looks like the weather on the lagoon; it is the emotional sense, a manner lacking warmth.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the emotional sense: a manner with no personal warmth is cold.

entries.clue: Mechanics stripped fasteners beneath sump (3,4)

indicators.note: the outside letters are stripped off
in a down clue this part comes below the next

blocks.note: a sump is a pit where liquid collects
SCREWS without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Mechanics find stripped screws under a car's oil sump.
annotation.walkthrough: Here 'stripped' does not mean a worn screw thread: it takes the outer letters off SCREWS.
annotation.definitionFit: A pit crew is the team of mechanics servicing a racing car.

entries.clue: Layer bearing wide cut (4)

indicators.note: carrying, so holding the other part inside

blocks.note: a hen is an egg layer
W is wide in cricket

annotation.surface: A layer containing a broad cut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Layer' is not a stratum but something that lays: a hen. In cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach.
annotation.definitionFit: Hewn means cut, as timber or stone is.

entries.clue: Plain papers kept in case (7)

indicators.note: placed inside the other part

blocks.note: in case of an event
identity papers

annotation.surface: Ordinary documents stored in a folder.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plain' reads as ordinary paper; it means obvious. 'Case' here is an occurrence, an event, not a box.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'plain' in the sense of clear or obvious, as in 'it was plain to everyone'.

entries.clue: Sign that insect’s entered outhouse (4-2)

indicators.note: has gone into the other part

blocks.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
an ant is an insect; the 's is 'has'

annotation.surface: A notice warns that an insect has got into the shed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sign' looks like a notice on the shed door; it is a star sign.
annotation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a shed built against a wall, an outhouse.

entries.clue: Assemble gun beside that woman (6)

indicators.note: the parts sit next to each other

blocks.note: gat is old slang for a gun
that woman is her

annotation.surface: Putting a gun together next to a woman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Assemble' reads as putting the gun together in the surface; as the definition it means to bring together or collect.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to bring things or people together in one place.

entries.clue: Rustic wooden frame is found in middle of wheelhouse (8)

indicators.note: IS goes inside the other part
the central letters of 'wheelhouse'

blocks.note: a yoke is the wooden frame joining oxen
the central two letters of wheeLHouse
used as it stands

annotation.surface: A rough wooden frame sits in the middle of a ship's wheelhouse.
annotation.walkthrough: In 'is found in', 'is' is fodder as well as the start of the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Yokelish means like a yokel, a country bumpkin: rustic.

entries.clue: Man is one heard somewhere in supermarket (4)

indicators.note: what you hear, not what is written

blocks.note: an aisle is a walkway between the shelves

annotation.surface: A man is heard somewhere in the supermarket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea, not a person.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Man, in the Irish Sea, is one of the British Isles.

entries.clue: Concocted porky pies after losing both leads for dogs (7)

indicators.note: made up, so the letters are rearranged
each word loses its first letter

blocks.clueFragment: porky pies after losing both leads
blocks.note: PORKY and PIES each lose their P

annotation.surface: Made-up porky pies with the dogs' leads gone.
annotation.walkthrough: Porky pies is rhyming slang for lies, so 'concocted porky pies' is a neat fit. Leads here are first letters, not dog leashes.
annotation.definitionFit: Yorkies are Yorkshire terriers, small dogs.

entries.clue: Maybe future ahead makes us become anxious (5,2)

blocks.note: the future is one grammatical tense
a team that is ahead is up

annotation.surface: Thinking about what lies ahead makes us worried.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Maybe future' is an example: the future is one grammatical tense.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: when nerves take hold the body stiffens, so becoming anxious is described this way.

entries.clue: Novelist‘s wife makes changes to yarn – not on! (6,5)

indicators.note: 'not on' says the word should be without ON, so those two letters are dropped from it

blocks.note: W is wife
to change is to alter
COTTON without ON

annotation.surface: A novelist's wife keeps changing his story, and he objects.
annotation.walkthrough: The ‘s is 'is' joining definition to wordplay. 'Yarn' suggests a story, but it is cotton thread.
annotation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Scott was the Scottish novelist who wrote Ivanhoe.
